plan.angle: Title: 'Do Semaglutide-Type Drugs Affect Macular Degeneration? #shorts'. If the class wording reads too vague, use 'GLP-1 Drugs Like Semaglutide and Macular Degeneration'. Name the drug class correctly in the narration: 'GLP-1 medicines, the class that includes semaglutide and tirzepatide'. Answer within 10 s: 'In a huge records study presented at the eye academy's October 2026 meeting, GLP-1 users at first had higher odds of macular degeneration, 1.68 times. When researchers adjusted for diabetes, blood pressure or cholesterol one at a time, the odds dropped below 1. Adjusting for age pushed them higher again. So it's linked, then unlinked, depending on the math: not proof of harm or protection.' Give each figure with its label ('crude', 'adjusted for diabetes', and so on). Explain confounding in one line. On screen: 'case-control · observational · conference abstract, not peer-reviewed (AAO, Oct 2026) · GLP-1 class · not shown to harm or protect'. Optionally add the peer-reviewed Ophthalmology 2026 semaglutide study, but only with figures checked against the paper. Separate line: the EMA lists NAION, a sudden loss of vision in one eye, as a very rare side effect of semaglutide. Action: keep regular eye exams, and get urgent care for any sudden vision change. One GI line: nausea, diarrhoea and constipation are common. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.' Full prescriber line. 170 words or fewer, no emoji.

plan.why: Fresh (Oct 21), low-competition, evidence-first correction of an eye-safety worry. Body-effect topics do well on Instagram, and eye topics reached 47 views on YouTube and 53 on Instagram. | fact-check: Major scope error. The AAO 2026 abstract (Ruan et al., Carle Illinois; AAO meeting Oct 9–12, 2026, New Orleans; Epic Cosmos, more than 300M patients) studied GLP-1 receptor agonists as a class, not semaglutide. The title and the 'semaglutide users' line misattribute it. The angle is also too tidy. Crude ORs: any AMD 1.68, dry 1.89, wet 1.53. Each adjustment was a single-factor Mantel-Haenszel adjustment: diabetes 0.69 (any) / 0.62 (wet), high blood pressure 0.65/0.59, high cholesterol 0.63/0.57. But adjusting for BMI only weakened it to 1.17, and adjusting for age raised it to 1.94. 'The link reversed' leaves out the factors that pushed the other way. The honest takeaway is that the result depends on which factor is adjusted for, so this abstract can't tell us either way. It is an unreviewed conference abstract. A separate peer-reviewed study (Ophthalmology 2026, Johns Hopkins, semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes) reported no statistical link to wet AMD. I couldn't open its full text (403), so the scriptwriter must confirm that study's figures before using any of them. The NAION line is fine: per EMA wording, 'very rare' with semaglutide. Keep it separate from AMD.

package.description:
Semaglutide and macular degeneration? A 2026 AAO conference abstract (not peer-reviewed) studied GLP-1 medicines as a class: unadjusted 1.68x the odds of any macular degeneration vs non-users. Adjusted one at a time for diabetes, blood pressure or cholesterol: below 1. For BMI or age: above 1. That's confounding, not proof of harm or protection.
In June 2025, EMA named NAION (sudden vision loss in one eye) a very rare semaglutide side effect. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting.
Keep regular eye exams; for sudden vision change, get urgent care and tell your prescriber.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

A 2026 AAO conference abstract looked at GLP-1 medicines as a class (not any one drug) using health records.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number against the sources and they all match. The Medical Xpress/HealthDay report of the AAO 2026 abstract (Ruan, Carle Illinois; New Orleans, Oct 9–12, 2026) is a case-control study using Epic Cosmos records. It looked at GLP-1 receptor agonists as a class, didn't report individual drugs, and hasn't been peer-reviewed. Its figures for any AMD are: unadjusted OR 1.68; 0.69 after accounting for type 2 diabetes, 0.65 for hypertension and 0.63 for hyperlipidemia (Mantel-Haenszel). The article says only that the OR was "attenuated to 1.17 with adjustment for body mass index" and that age "was associated with an increase in odds ratios to 1.94". It doesn't name the AMD subtype for those two, and the script's narration correctly doesn't name one either. EMA PRAC (2–5 June 2025 meeting, highlights dated 6 June 2025) concluded that NAION is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (up to 1 in 10,000). The Ozempic EPAR (last updated 25/08/2026) lists diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea as the most common side effects. The framing is good: the confounding is explained, nothing is claimed as harm or protection, the class-versus-single-drug scope is stated, and the safety lines and prescriber line are there. The fixes below are minor wording changes.

issues.claim: Adjusted for BMI alone: 1.17 / Adjusted for age alone: 1.94
issues.problem: The source doesn't say "alone" for these two, and it doesn't say whether they refer to any, dry or wet AMD. A muted viewer could read them as any-AMD single-factor results, which is more than the source states.
issues.fix: Replace the items with: "Odds ratios vs non-users, as reported (HealthDay); AMD type not specified", "Adjusted for BMI: 1.17", "Adjusted for age: 1.94"

issues.problem: The source says "Mantel-Haenszel adjustment after accounting for" each factor, listed separately. "One at a time" is a fair reading, but it's an inference.
issues.fix: Change the narration to: "Adjusted for diabetes, point six nine. Blood pressure, point six five. Cholesterol, point six three." Keep the on-screen items as they are, but change "alone" to "(reported separately)".

issues.claim: Europe's regulator called NAION ... a very rare semaglutide side effect
issues.problem: The conclusion came from the EMA's safety committee (PRAC). The house rules say to credit the exact body.
issues.fix: Change the narration to: "In June twenty twenty-five, the European Medicines Agency's safety committee concluded NAION, sudden vision loss in one eye, is a very rare semaglutide side effect."

issues.problem: In an eye-focused Short, the EPAR also lists a semaglutide eye effect: serious worsening of diabetic retinopathy, which can affect up to 1 in 10 people. Mentioning it briefly keeps the eye-safety picture complete for viewers with type 2 diabetes.
issues.fix: Add to the s9 items, tagged to src3: "With diabetes: diabetic retinopathy can worsen; keep eye checks (EMA)". Optionally add to the narration: "If you have diabetes, diabetic eye disease can worsen, so keep your eye checks."
